The next low tide is at 8:48pm (NOAA, station 9414290). Today's high was 5.2 ft at 1:34pm. I don't have a live sea temperature or the latest NPS alerts right now.

It's plover season, so dogs need a six-foot leash in the Snowy Plover Protection Area, the southern stretch of the beach, through May 15 ([NPS Ocean Beach](https://www.nps.gov/goga/planyourvisit/oceanbeach.htm)).

results.ask: I want to do a bonfire at the beach Saturday
results.expect: includes plover season status and fire rules with sources, unprompted; cites
results.answer:
Not this Saturday, or any Saturday until March. Beach bonfires are banned from November 1 through February 28 to avoid Spare the Air days, per the [NPS Ocean Beach page](https://www.nps.gov/goga/planyourvisit/oceanbeach.htm) and [NPS beach fire rules](https://www.nps.gov/goga/learn/management/fire_beachfireregs.htm). When fires are allowed, they're only in the provided fire rings between Stairwells 15 and 20.

Plovers are also on the beach now. Their protection season runs through May 15, 2027, so any dogs need a six-foot leash in the protection area ([NPS](https://www.nps.gov/goga/planyourvisit/oceanbeach.htm)).

For a beach gathering now, the [Surfrider Foundation San Francisco](https://sf.surfrider.org/) runs beach cleanups, which is a good way to meet people on the sand.

results.ask: What's special about my block? I'm on 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega.
results.expect: calls about_block; gives the block's own figures and something pinned nearby, with sources; cites
results.answer:
Your block sits about 39 feet above sea level, 0.2 miles from Ocean Beach. Most homes went up around 1941, and the city's roll has some dating to 1908 and others as late as 2004 ([SF Assessor-Recorder, via DataSF](https://data.sf.gov/d/yhqp-riqs)).

- **Right at your corner:** OpenSFHistory pins two old photos about 250 feet north, at 46th and Moraga, from the [Western Neighborhoods Project archive](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.929.jpg) and [another](https://opensfhistory.org/Display/wnp58.923.jpg).
- **About 950 feet east:** Henry Doelger's Rainbow House (1941) and Freedom House (1942) were model homes with hopeful names, built just before wartime rules halted building ([SF Planning, Sunset historic context](https://default.sfplanning.org/Preservation/sunset_survey/Adopted_SunsetHCS.pdf)).

Street sweeping: east side Mondays 1st and 3rd, next on Nov 16; west side Thursdays 1st, 3rd, and 5th, next on Nov 19, both noon to 2pm ([SF street sweeping schedule](https://data.sf.gov/d/yhqp-riqs)). The posted signs are the last word.

If you know your block's history, I'd like to hear it. You can share it for the notes.

results.ask: When is street cleaning on 46th between Moraga and Noriega?
results.expect: calls about_block; gives each side's days and hours, names the source, says the signs are the last word; cites
results.answer:
On 46th Ave between Moraga and Noriega, street cleaning is on two schedules, one for each side:

- **East side:** Mondays on the 1st and 3rd weeks, noon to 2pm. Next: Monday, November 16, 2026.
- **West side:** Thursdays on the 1st, 3rd, and 5th weeks, noon to 2pm. Next: Thursday, November 19, 2026.

Neither side is cleaned on city holidays. This comes from the [SF street sweeping schedule](https://data.sf.gov/d/yhqp-riqs). The signs on the block are the last word, so read them when you park.

results.ask: I want to make a street cleaning reminder for my block. Is there already something like that?
results.expect: searches first; points to what exists (the city's schedule, the block's days) rather than proposing a build; cites
results.answer:
I don't have a reminder tool, so nothing here will text or email you. The closest thing is the [SF Public Works street sweeping schedule](https://sfpublicworks.org/services/mechanical-street-sweeping-and-street-cleaning-schedule), which lists cleaning days block by block. Look up your block there and set your own phone or calendar reminder. Holidays can change the days, so check the [SFMTA holiday list](https://www.sfmta.com/getting-around/drive-park/holiday-enforcement-schedule) too.

If you give me your block's cross streets (for example, "Judah between 45th and 46th"), I can pull up its cleaning days and the next date from the city's data.
